Bug_Title: Optional value should only be accessed after calling isPresent()
Bug_Explanation: The bug is due to accessing the value of an Optional directly using get() without first checking if the value is present using isPresent(). This can lead to a NoSuchElementException if the Optional is empty.
Trigger_Explanation: The generated JUnit test cases call the methods showBug() and showBug2() from the OptionalAccessExample class. Both methods attempt to access the value of an Optional using the get() method without first verifying that the value is present using isPresent(). This leads to a NoSuchElementException being thrown, which causes the JUnit tests to fail, thus effectively triggering the bug.
